explain.say: Your body works best at about 37 degrees Celsius. When you get too hot, one of its main ways to cool down is sweating.

explain.say: A part of the brain called the hypothalamus works like a thermostat. When it senses your blood warming up, it sends nerve signals to millions of sweat glands in your skin.

explain.say: The glands pour watery sweat onto your skin. At the same time, blood vessels near the skin widen, bringing warm blood to the surface, which is why you look flushed.

explain.say: The cooling happens when the sweat evaporates. Turning liquid water into vapour takes a lot of heat energy, and that heat is taken from your skin and the blood beneath it.

faq.a: Sweat cools you when it evaporates. Changing from liquid to vapour needs energy, which is taken as heat from your skin, so the skin and the blood flowing under it cool down.
The hypothalamus, a small area at the base of the brain, acts as the body's thermostat. When body temperature rises it signals the sweat glands to work.
asks: Tell me about the brain thermostat

faq.q: Why is sweating less useful on humid days?
faq.a: When the air is already full of water vapour, sweat evaporates slowly. It drips off instead of evaporating, so it takes away much less heat.
asks: Why do I feel hotter when it is humid?

faq.q: How many sweat glands do we have?
faq.a: People have roughly 2 to 4 million sweat glands, with many on the palms, soles and forehead.
Sweat is mostly water with some salt and small amounts of other substances. It has almost no smell; body odour comes from skin bacteria breaking down sweat from certain glands.

facts: Humans have roughly 2 to 4 million sweat glands.
Evaporating sweat removes heat because water absorbs energy as it turns into vapour.

quiz.say: What actually cools your skin when you sweat?
quiz.show: What actually cools your skin when you sweat?
quiz.why: Evaporation takes heat energy from the skin.

wrong.0: Sweat comes out at body temperature; it is not cold.
wrong.2: Salt does not cool you; the water evaporating does.
